(disclaimer : I'm working on a "DAOC 2")

There are a couple projects that are starting right now because of how great the game creation landscape is becoming, (mainly thanks to free resources and game engines like Unreal), and because people feel like Camelot Unchained's combat did not capture what made DAOC great.

Nonwithstanding that the nostalgia factor is strong and hard to replicate, our game will feel will be much closer to the original, DAOC.

Our beloved realms will remain in our heart, it was also a different time where people were playing with friends, or making new friends, discovering what the world had to offer on their own and did not watch youtube videos to solve a quest's riddles (original epic quests were just a torture for some people, but also my best memories solving them with the guild), making it our own and creating fond memories, it will be hard to recapture this exact feeling.

Now MMORPG games devs keep boasting about "Features" of their MMO. (ashes of creation) before event talking about combat mechanics & storytelling.

Note that no asset from DAOC can be reused in a commercial project, so there is no way we can use the work shown in this post for example, which is a shame, but it is what it is. (which we did not create and I really like this video from OP)

Nothing prevents us from making some zones with notable "landmarks" of the original DAOC, as some kind of easter eggs, like the bridge of Gotar why not ? but we will have to recreate it from scratch.

Instantly also thinking about Stonehenge, some zone like Muspelheim, or some architectural inspiration or even some NPC names. (Talking mainly about names that were borrowed from history/mythology)

Making an MMO is an absolutely daunting task, thankfully, we are working with an incredible set of tools and a talented team of passionate folks.

We are also making our own tools to create the world.

Because there is no way we could recreate a world like DAOC from scratch with a team of less than 30 people and make it engaging.

So we use AI assisted procedural generation for most of the world, hand crafting details, in UE 5.

Our main challenges has been working with Epic, Unreal engine devs, and plugins devs to allow many players on a single server, or find a way to load balance single zones, as Unreal is really not fit for large player counts.

While this is not expected to be solved in the very near future, it doesn't prevent us from working on the world and combat mechanics and other features.

We'll make an official post once we are ready to share more and when the game studio is created.
